value.lineage: Go-Explore (Ecoffet, Huizinga, Lehman, Stanley, Clune 2019/2021): archive-based exploration -- remember cells, return to them, explore from them, then robustify

HUMAN_PROBLEM.value: detachment and derailment in exploration: remembering where you have been and going back on purpose

value.built_to: solve hard-exploration reinforcement-learning problems (Montezuma's Revenge, Pitfall) by keeping an archive of visited states ('cells'), deterministically returning to promising cells, exploring from them, and later robustifying the discovered trajectories into a policy
value.pressure: sparse and deceptive rewards where naive exploration forgets promising states and never returns to them; the environment punishes detachment and derailment
value.success_means: reaching previously unreached game states and scores; in the paper, surpassing the human world record on Montezuma's Revenge and solving all Atari hard-exploration games

cut.note: exploration as an archive: states are mapped to coarse cells; each cell remembers the best score, the trajectory length, and a RESTORABLE emulator snapshot; a cycle selects cells by count-based weights, restores each, explores randomly from it, and adds or replaces cells when a trajectory reaches a new cell or the same cell with a better score or a shorter path; the cell representation itself can be re-fitted during the run (dynamic downscaling); robustification (turning the archive's trajectories into a policy) is a separate phase, not in this directory

organs.human_name: class Cell (167-255): score, seen_times, chosen_times, chosen_since_new, action_times, trajectory_len, restore, traj_last, real_cell, cell_frame; self.grid (a dict keyed by the cell key); Discretizer / GridDimension (82-166) for domain-specific keys
organs.mechanism: a cell key is a discretisation of the state (a downscaled, quantised frame, or domain attributes such as room and position); the archive maps keys to Cell records; a record stores the emulator state needed to return to the cell (restore), the best score reached there, the length of the trajectory that reached it, the id of its last experience step (for reconstructing trajectories from the experience arrays), and four counters used by selection and reset on update
organs.input: visited states with their emulator snapshots
assumptions: returning to a state is possible (a deterministic emulator with save/restore) so exploration never has to re-learn how to get somewhere; a coarse key groups similar states so the archive stays small
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the exploration frontier is stored, not re-discovered; detachment and derailment (the paper's two failure modes of intrinsic motivation) do not arise
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the archive is only as good as the cell representation; the restore snapshot makes it emulator-bound (the policy_based/ directory exists because of that)
organs.human_prior: Ecoffet et al. 2019/2021; the archive is the paper's central object

organs.human_name: randselectors.WeightedSelector (52-144): Weight(weight, power) for seen, chosen, action, room_cells, chosen_since_new; DirWeights; cell_update maintaining all_weights, cell_score, possible_scores and cached_pos_weights; choose_cell(grid, size)
organs.mechanism: each cell's selection weight is a product of terms of the form weight / (count + 1)^power over its counters (seen, chosen, chosen since it last produced a new cell, actions taken from it), optionally with domain terms (neighbouring cells in a direction, level, doors); weights are cached per cell and recomputed only for the cell that changed and for its possible neighbours (by score); a batch of cells is drawn proportionally to weight
assumptions: cells visited or chosen less often are more likely to lead somewhere new (a count-based novelty prior); the caches make selection cheap as the archive grows
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: exploration effort spread over the frontier rather than concentrated where the score is
organs.failure_landscape: UNKNOWN by run; by reading: the weights' powers and constants are per-game settings (experiment_settings.py, 1,491 lines)

organs.human_name: run_cycle (861-1011): selector.choose_cell; POOL.map(process_cell) restores and explores; the trajectory walk with seen_cells; should_accept_cell (1012-1020); the update block (restore, score, trajectory_len, traj_last, cell_frame); reset_cell_on_update
organs.mechanism: per cycle: draw a batch of cells; in worker processes restore each cell's snapshot and run the explorer (random actions) for a bounded number of steps recording every step's cell, reward and snapshot; back in the main process walk each trajectory: increment seen counts (once per cell per trajectory), append to the experience arrays, and when a step lands in a cell that is new, or has a higher score, or the same score with a shorter trajectory, overwrite that cell's record (snapshot, score, length, frame) and zero the start cell's chosen-since-new; optionally zero all counters of updated cells so they are re-explored
organs.output: an updated archive and appended experience
assumptions: exploring from a returned-to state with random actions is enough to find new cells (the 'exploration is easy once you can return' claim); shorter trajectories to the same cell are preferable for later robustification
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: Montezuma's Revenge and Pitfall solved by exploration alone (the paper's result); the archive's trajectories are the demonstrations for the second phase
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the accept rule prefers score, so a longer trajectory with a higher score displaces a shorter one; ignore_death trims the last steps of a trajectory that ended in death

organs.human_name: try_split_frames / maybe_split_dynamic_state (464-693): random_recent_frames, get_dist_score (entropy normalised by a target length), geometric proposals for shape and pixel depth, the grid re-keying with counter carry-over (662-670)
organs.mechanism: a reservoir of recent frames is periodically re-discretised under candidate (shape, pixel-depth) parameters proposed geometrically around the current best; a candidate is scored by the entropy of the induced cell distribution penalised by its distance from a target number of cells; the best parameters replace the current ones and the archive is re-keyed, merging cells and carrying their counters and best records over
organs.output: new parameters and a re-keyed archive
assumptions: a good representation splits the visited states into neither too few nor too many cells; entropy against a target size is a usable proxy without domain knowledge
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the domain-agnostic variant of the paper (no hand-made room/position key)
organs.source_boundary: the two functions; CANDIDATE because the proposal loop was skimmed

pressures.source_evidence: goexplore.py run_cycle; randselectors.py; the paper's ablations as cited in the README
pressures.condition: an organism acts in a deterministic environment with save/restore; rewards are rare and locally misleading; the score is the number of distinct far states reached (and the best score) per environment step; the state space is huge but coarsely clusterable
pressures.resource_or_constraint: environment steps; archive memory; the coarseness of the key
pressures.failure_condition: detachment (forgetting how to reach a frontier) or derailment (failing to return before exploring), or an archive that grows without reaching new places
pressures.world_punishes: intrinsic-motivation exploration that must re-traverse; keys too fine (no coverage) or too coarse (no frontier)
pressures.world_rewards: an archive with restore, count-based selection, and a representation tuned to a target cell count
pressures.observable_consequence: cells discovered and best score vs environment steps on Montezuma's Revenge with selection uniform vs count-weighted, and with the key fixed vs refitted
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: a state enumerator (which the world must make infeasible by size)
pressures.cheat_control: an organism given the map of far states must reach them in the minimum steps; the archive with restore disabled (must re-traverse) must show derailment; uniform selection must show slower coverage than count-weighted: the world must show all three
pressures.purpose_separated_from_pressure: PURPOSE: hard-exploration reinforcement learning (Ecoffet et al. 2019-2021)
